html:
The Baltic tribes, or Balts, were the peoples who spoke Baltic languages along the south-eastern shore of the Baltic Sea. On the map for 800 to 1000 they hold the coast and forests from the Vistula to the Gulf of Riga. They included the Old Prussians, Curonians, Semigallians, Latgalians, Yotvingians and Lithuanians.

They farmed, kept cattle, fished and lived in villages under wooden hill forts. Amber from their coast had been traded south since Roman times along the Amber Road. In the Viking Age Scandinavians raided and traded along the coast, and Islamic coins, part of the flow of Samanid silver, turn up in their hoards. They kept their own gods long after their neighbours became Christian.

That ended with the Northern Crusades of the 1200s. The Teutonic Knights conquered the Prussians and Livonia. Only the Lithuanians built a strong state of their own, Lithuania, and stayed pagan until it was baptised in 1387.
